items.stem: You run Remove Duplicates on a Name column, but 'ACME' and 'acme' both remain. Why?

options.text: Power Query compares text case-sensitively, so the two values are treated as different
options.rationale: Correct: apply an upper/lower-case transform before removing duplicates when case should not matter.

options.text: Remove Duplicates only works on numbers
options.rationale: It works on text columns too.

options.text: The column must be sorted first
options.rationale: Sorting is not required for Remove Duplicates.

options.text: Duplicates can only be removed across all columns
options.rationale: You can remove duplicates on a subset of columns.

items.explanation: Correct: apply an upper/lower-case transform before removing duplicates when case should not matter.

items.stem: Which TWO are true about removing duplicates in Power Query? (Select TWO.)

options.text: There is no guarantee which duplicate row is kept
options.rationale: Correct: folding and optimisation mean the retained instance is not guaranteed; buffer first for predictability.

options.text: Table.Buffer can make removal behave predictably
options.rationale: Correct: buffering the table first fixes the row order before de-duplication.

options.text: Removing duplicates always reduces memory use
options.rationale: If the step cannot fold to the source it can significantly increase memory use.

options.text: Duplicates can only be evaluated on a single column
options.rationale: Duplication can be tested across any chosen subset of columns.

items.explanation: Correct: folding and optimisation mean the retained instance is not guaranteed; buffer first for predictability.

items.stem: You fix a few bad values directly in the Power Query data preview instead of adding a transform step. What is the main problem?

options.text: The change is not recorded as a step, so the query will not reproduce it on refresh
options.rationale: Correct: reproducibility depends on recorded applied steps, not manual edits.

options.text: Power Query does not allow editing values
options.rationale: It does, but ad-hoc edits still should be steps.

options.text: It permanently alters the source file
options.rationale: Power Query does not write back to the source.

options.text: It converts the query to a static table
options.rationale: The query remains refreshable; the manual fix just is not captured.

items.explanation: Correct: reproducibility depends on recorded applied steps, not manual edits.
